overview: This bill names the federal building at 300 West Congress Street in Tucson, Arizona, the 'Raul M. Grijalva Federal Building.' Any reference to the building in federal laws, maps or records would use the new name. Naming federal buildings is a common way Congress honors public figures, and the bill does not change how the building is used or funded. As of October 29, 2025, a Senate committee had approved it and it was placed on the Senate's calendar, meaning it is eligible for a vote by the full Senate.
for: Supporters say naming the building honors a long record of public service to the Tucson community.
against: Critics say the bill is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
